issues.legal_issue: Income-tax assessment and appellate orders are not conclusive proof of the lawfulness of income sources and cannot, by themselves, justify quashing a disproportionate-assets prosecution or discharging the accused.

Exoneration in tax proceedings does not bar a criminal prosecution under the Prevention of Corruption Act when the proceedings concern different statutory issues, authorities, and scopes of adjudication.

A charge may be framed where material on record gives rise to strong suspicion that the accused committed the offence; the court need not conduct a trial or assess whether the evidence would secure conviction at that stage.
A person’s minority during part of the alleged check period does not, by itself, justify quashing charges where the person was an adult during another part of that period.
